title: 2026 gift-tax annual exclusion + estate basic exclusion
description: 2026 IRS join: $19,000 annual gift exclusion per donee, $194,000 non-citizen-spouse annual exclusion, $15,000,000 basic exclusion for estate/gift/GST. From IR-2025-103, Rev. Proc. 2025-32, and IRC §2010 as amended by P.L. 119-21. Not tax advice.
extract: For calendar year 2026 the IRS annual exclusion for gifts to any one person stays at $19,000 (same as 2025). The annual exclusion for gifts to a spouse who is not a U.S. citizen is $194,000 (up from $190,000). Estates of decedents who die in 2026 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,000,000, up from $13,990,000 for 2025 deaths. Public Law 119-21 (Working Families Tax Cuts / OBBBA §70106) set that $15,000,000 figure in IRC §2010(c)(3) for 2026; inflation adjustment resumes for 2027. The generation-skipping transfer exemption for 2026 equals the same $15,000,000. Spouses who elect gift-splitting can combine two $19,000 annual exclusions to the same donee. A gift above the annual exclusion generally requires Form 709 even when no tax is due because the excess uses lifetime applicable exclusion. This page joins the annual-exclusion table and the basic-exclusion history on one URL. Compiled 2026-08-29. Not tax, estate, or legal advice.

faq.q: What is the 2026 annual gift-tax exclusion?
faq.a: IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 keeps the 2026 annual exclusion at $19,000 per donee, the same dollar amount as 2025.

faq.q: What is the 2026 estate-tax basic exclusion?
faq.a: Estates of decedents who die in 2026 have a basic exclusion of $15,000,000. IRS IR-2025-103 and the estate/gift whats new page cite P.L. 119-21 §70106.

faq.q: Does a gift over $19,000 automatically create tax?
faq.a: Usually it creates a filing duty on Form 709. Tax is due only after lifetime applicable exclusion is used up. Confirm with Form 709 instructions.
